text: I ran 6 moderated usability sessions on our transit trip planner prototype and ended up with about 30 observation notes, one per sticky, each tagged with which participant. normally we'd affinity map on the whiteboard but the lab whiteboard got wiped (again) so I want something local in the browser. notes scattered on a canvas, I drag them into groups, each group gets a name that becomes a theme. colour each note by participant so we can see if a theme is really just one person

dragging works but the groups are only visual. it needs to know which notes are in which cluster: drop a note on a cluster and it joins, drag it out and it leaves. moving a cluster should bring its notes with it. and a list of themes on the side with how many notes and how many participants each
can I zoom out? with 30 notes it doesnt fit on my laptop screen. ctrl+scroll and +/- buttons, and a fit-all. also arrow keys to nudge the selected note, dragging is fiddly for small moves
clicking a theme in the side list should highlight its notes on the board and dim everything else. and rename a cluster by double clicking its title, right now I cant change 'Untitled' at all
add a new cluster button and let me resize clusters, some themes are big. then export the themes with their notes as markdown so I can paste them straight into the report, unsorted notes at the end
